summary: Albert Debrunner was a linguist and Indologist. He held posts at the University of Zurich (circa 1903–1907), Basel (circa 1918–1920), Greifswald (circa 1920–1927), Jena (circa 1927–1935), and Bern (circa 1935–1954).

Albert Grünwedel was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (circa 1876–1882) and served as Direktor at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from circa 1883 to 1921.

Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as a professor at the University of Greifswald from circa 1840 to 1883 and founded the Zeitschrift für die Wissenschaft der Sprache in 1845.

Albert Thumb was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg (circa 1884–1888). He later held academic posts at Freiburg (circa 1889–1909) and the University of Marburg (circa 1909–1915).

Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara and Yun-hua Jan, later serving at the University of Winnipeg and University of Arizona.

Albion Moonlight Butters specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and Columbia University, completing his PhD under Robert A. F. Thurman along with several traditional teachers.

Albrecht Hanisch is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He held posts at the Nepal Research Centre and the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Albrecht Weber was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Breslau, Bonn, and Berlin under scholars including Stenzler, Lassen, and Kuhn. He held several posts at Humboldt University of Berlin and the Prussian Academy of Sciences.

Albrecht Wezler was an Indologist who studied at the University of Tübingen under Paul Thieme. He served as Director at the University of Hamburg and Director General of the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1982–2002).
Alec M. Terrana studied religious studies and Buddhist studies at Pomona College, completing a BA in 2014 with Zhiru Ng on his committee.

Aleix Ruiz-Falqués is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Eivind Kahrs and held posts at Shan State Buddhist University and Singapore University of Technology and Design.

Alessandro Graheli works in Indology and philosophy. By 2022, he was a university assistant at the University of Vienna and a principal investigator at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.
Alex McKay works in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from SOAS University of London in 1995 and held a research fellowship at University College London.

Alex Watson works in Indology and philosophy. Educated at Oxford and SOAS, he completed his doctorate under Alexis Sanderson and Harunaga Isaacson, later holding posts at Wolfson College, Harvard University, and Ashoka University.

Alex Wayman was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at UCLA and UC Berkeley. He taught at the University of Michigan, the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and Columbia University (1966–1991).

Alexander Berzin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rutgers, Princeton, and Harvard University, and trained under traditional teachers including Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Dudjom Rinpoche.

Alexander Coburn Soper specialized in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology. After studying at Hamilton College and Princeton University, he held academic posts at Bryn Mawr College (circa 1939–1960) and New York University (circa 1960–1993).

Alexander Csoma de Kőrös was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen and under traditional teachers in Ladakh, later serving as sub-librarian at the Asiatic Society (circa 1837–1842).

Alexander Gardner is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. and holds a post at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.
Alexander James O'Neill is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He is a PhD candidate at the University of Toronto and a research fellow at Taisho University.
